conviction_note: The findings lean positive (+0.6 sum). Management has said twice that it booked only a small part of the favourable risk-adjustment/morbidity signal, Oscar has raised its 2026 operating guide twice since July, and the Q3 marketplace commentary from Centene and Molina is benign. Against that, the stock is up 16.7% in 5 days to a 52-week high with upside calls already bid, and on the near-identical Q2 setup (big beat plus raise) a +20% pre-market spike reversed to -11.86% on churn worries. So p_up sits barely above 50 (52) on an abs_move of 10, slightly above the 9.62% implied because the Q3 call is the first venue for 2027 colour. The scaled number is +0.4 and the sum is +0.6. The two agree in sign and the small gap is the reaction-function discount.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS about -$0.22 (Chartmill https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/OSCR/estimates, and iTiger preview 2026-10-29 https://www.itiger.com/news/1158806314, which also gives EBIT of about -$62.6m and revenue of about $4.72bn) against -$0.25 and revenue of $4.73bn (Benzinga, as summarised in search results). Chartmill gives revenue of $4.818bn. Two sources agree within $0.03 on EPS, so the bar counts as sourced. Company FY2026 guide, raised 2026-09-16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000074/oscr-20260916.htm): earnings from operations $600-800m, MLR 81.0-82.0%, revenue $18.7-19.0bn, SG&A ratio 15.6-16.1%. H1 earnings from operations were $704.1m in Q1 plus $388.6m in Q2, $1,092.7m in total, so the guide implies an H2 operating LOSS of $293-493m. H1 revenue of $9.53bn implies $9.17-9.47bn for H2, about $4.59-4.74bn a quarter. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on EPS: my read is about -$0.13 against -$0.22, i.e. +40% of the absolute bar. The number is uncertain and the name trades on MLR, earnings from operations and the guide rather than on EPS precision.
positioning_check: Short interest is 16.45m shares with 2.7 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (massive.com quote page dated 2026-10-26, https://massive.com/quote/oscr). Curvedtrading shows 16.4m and 2.3 days at the 2026-08-14 settlement, down from 17.8m and 4.1 days on 2026-07-31 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/oscr/short-interest/). Chartmill's undated float-short figure is 7.79%. The short is not crowded. Baseline skew_25d is -3.35 vol points (calls priced above puts, 'upside paid'), the put/call OI ratio is 0.38, the event-implied move is 9.62%, ATM IV is 140.5%, the 5-day run-up is +16.7%, the 20-day run-up is +8.08%, and the stock sits at its 52-week high. Taken together, options and tape already lean long into the print. Sell-side tone in the 2026-10-29 iTiger preview is described as mostly bearish (BofA Underperform $30, UBS Neutral, Goldman Hold, Barclays Buy, with a Barclays PT of $49 after the investor day).

findings.finding: Management has twice said it recognised only part of the favourable 2026 market-morbidity and risk-adjustment signal. On Q1 (2026-05-06) Bertolini said claims were better than expected but 'we have not booked all of that', and RA reserves were still set on pricing morbidity. On Q2 (2026-08-06) CFO Blackley said Oscar recognised 'only a small portion' of the favourability in the first 2026 market report. Each quarter's beat has since been followed by a raised operating guide: $250-450m to $500-700m in August, then to $600-800m on 2026-09-16. A further release of that held-back accrual would land on Q3 earnings from operations against a consensus of about -$63m EBIT and -$0.22 EPS, and could take the FY guide above $600-800m (the Q3 call is the next venue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beat and raise: Q1 2026 (EPS $2.07, guide reaffirmed with a 'meet or exceed' stance) bought +10.59%. Q2 2026 (EPS $1.10 vs $0.43, operating guide raised $250m) spiked more than 20% pre-market and closed -11.86% on H2 churn worries. The 2026-09-16 investor-day raise of +$100m bought about +2.4%. Q3 2025 beat: -2.76%. Beats on this line pay about half the time.
findings.why_not_priced: The size of the held-back accrual was never quantified, so consensus cannot model it. The iTiger preview of 2026-10-29 has consensus at a Q3 loss of -$0.22 and quotes UBS saying in-quarter upside is limited because the guide already embeds favourable utilisation. If the market had priced a further release, Q3 EPS estimates would sit near breakeven rather than at a loss and the sell-side mix would not read mostly bearish. Part of it is probably in the 16.7% five-day run-up and the call-bid skew, which is why this is sized well under the implied move.
findings.independence: The Q1 2026 transcript (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/06/oscar-health-oscr-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/, 2026-05-06) records the same 'not booked all of that' stance one quarter earlier; it is the same company, a different document and a different quarter. Q2 primary release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000066/oscarhealthsecondquarter20.htm, 2026-08-06): $164m favourable PPD and a guide raise, i.e. the mechanism has already paid out once.

findings.finding: Peer Q3 2026 marketplace prints that landed after Oscar last spoke (2026-09-16) show no repeat of the 2025 Q3 morbidity shock. Centene (2026-10-27): commercial/marketplace HBR 89.0% vs 89.9% a year earlier on 'improved pricing and risk transfer', marketplace 'on track', adjusted EPS floor raised $0.40 to >$5.20. Molina (Q3 2026 8-K): marketplace MCR 92.5%, 'in line with normal seasonality and expectations'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In 2025 the peer morbidity read-through drove the Q2 2025 guide cut (-11.6% on the July 2025 pre-announcement shown in baseline history as 2025-07-22 +7.93% / 2025-08-06 +3.76%; the market had already sold off). No clean history of OSCR reacting to benign peer reads at its own print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Both peers are public and Centene printed before the 5-day run-up began (2026-10-28 onward), so this is a confirming proxy and not a surprise. Kept small: if the market doubted the sector's Q3 MLR, OSCR would not be at a 52-week high with calls bid.
findings.independence: Molina Q3 2026 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000042/moh3q26_er.htm (marketplace MCR 92.5%, in line). Different company, different document. Both are proxies for Oscar's own MLR, not Oscar's number.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (2026-08-06) the CFO said H2 2026 monthly churn would run 'closer to twice' the earlier 1-2% assumption because of CMS eligibility verification. Membership already fell from 3.17m (2026-03-31) to 2.96m (2026-06-30). Q3 consensus revenue of $4.72-4.82bn sits at or above the $4.59-4.74bn a quarter implied by the unchanged FY revenue guide less H1, so the revenue and membership line carries miss risk. Membership attrition was the stated cause of the -11.86% Q2 reversal.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: a record profit and a raised guide closed -11.86% after a more than 20% pre-market spike, attributed to expected H2 membership churn (Kalkine, Parameter). Q3 2025 revenue missed ($2.99bn vs $3.09bn) and the stock moved -2.76%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the churn statement is three months old and drove the August sell-off. The unpriced part is that consensus revenue still sits at the top of what the unchanged revenue guide implies. If the market had marked revenue to the churn guidance, Q3 revenue estimates would cluster near $4.6bn, not $4.72-4.82bn. The offset is that peer Centene's marketplace members fell only 2.6% in Q3 (3.49m to 3.40m), which argues the attrition was milder than feared.
findings.independence: Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000066/oscarhealthsecondquarter20.htm): 2.963m members at 2026-06-30 against 3.17m at Q1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000036/oscarhealthfirstquarter202.htm). It shares the actuary.info document with finding 1 but rests on a different line (membership/revenue vs MLR/accrual). The counter-evidence is Centene's 3,403,300 vs 3,494,700 marketplace members (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001071739/000107173926000194/a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is long. The stock is +16.7% in 5 sessions and +8.1% in 20 to a 52-week high ($35.57), with no company 8-K since 2026-09-16 (EDGAR filing list) to explain the move. The 25-delta skew is -3.35 (calls over puts) and put/call OI is 0.38. On the near-identical Q2 setup the stock reversed from more than +20% pre-market to a -11.86% close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: good print, sold -11.86% at the close after a pre-market spike. 2025-05-07 (Q1 2025) +30.22% from a low base. Run-ups into prints have not been consistently rewarded on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: This finding is about the price itself. The skew and run-up show the bull case is held, so a beat without a raise above $800m (or without 2027 margin colour) has room to be sold, as in August. The baseline file (sealed 2026-11-04) carries the run-up and skew. Short interest is 2.7 days to cover, so there is no squeeze mechanism to offset it.
findings.independence: Baseline sealed tape and options (research/2026/11/2026-11-04/edge-split-2/baselines/OSCR.json). EDGAR filing list for CIK 1568651 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001568651&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) shows only Form 4s since the 2026-09-16 8-K, so the run-up has no company catalyst.

findings.finding: The 2027 setup gives the Q3 call room to raise the forward narrative. Oscar adds 140 counties (713 across 21 states, entering South Carolina) for 2027 (Healthcare Dive, 2026-10-21). Cigna is exiting the individual market in all 11 of its states and 11 carriers are exiting at least one state (KFF, 2026-10-30). The finalised average benchmark silver premium rises 13% for 2027. Against that, CBO projects marketplace enrollment falls to 13.1m in 2027 and BofA (Underperform, $30) doubts an enrollment recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 calls have historically carried next-year colour. Q3 2025 (2025-11-06, -2.76%) introduced the 2026 'return to profitability' narrative and the stock fell on the day. No clean positive precedent.
findings.why_not_priced: The facts are public, but no 2027 earnings number exists (the investor day gave only 2029 targets: 5-7% operating margin, $4+ EPS). Any 2027 margin or membership commentary on the call is new information whose sign is not set. Sized small because the direction is genuinely two-sided.
findings.independence: Healthcare Dive 2026-10-21 https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/centene-oscar-unitedhealthcare-new-counties-aca-2027/833442/ (Oscar +140 counties; carrier exits affect hundreds of thousands of enrollees). Different publisher, overlapping facts.

findings.finding: Supply overhang. Thrive Capital funds distributed about 6.3m Class A shares in kind to their LPs on 2026-09-18 (Form 4 and 13D/A filed that day), and executives filed Form 144s on 2026-09-03 followed by Form 4s on 2026-09-08, 09-22 and 10-13. The iTiger preview lists insider sales and the large-holder distribution as a watch item.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. The stock rose from about $33 to $35.57 after the distribution, so the supply appears absorbed.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the event is seven weeks old and the stock has since made new highs. Filed because distributed LP holders could sell into a post-print spike. The Oct 13 Form 4s were not opened, so their sale/grant nature is unverified.
findings.independence: iTiger preview 2026-10-29 https://www.itiger.com/news/1158806314 names insider sales and the large-holder distribution as a factor. That is a different source but the same facts.

outside_window.finding: 2027 open-enrollment plan selections (OE started 2026-11-01). CMS snapshots and Oscar's 2027 membership are not visible inside a one-session window.
Oscar's formal 2027 guidance has historically come with Q4 results in February (2026-02-10 release), not at the Q3 print.

searched_and_found_nothing: A cause for the +16.7% 5-day run-up (2026-10-28 to 11-04): no Oscar 8-K since 2026-09-16 on EDGAR, and no dated news, upgrade or ACA policy event found for that week
Wakely Q3 2026 (claims through mid-year) market-morbidity report: not publicly reachable; only the April 2026 white paper (17-26% enrollment decline, 2.9-6.5% morbidity rise) was found

Analyst price-target changes dated 2026-10-15 to 2026-11-04: none found

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into finding 1 and the bar. It is the bar for the accrual-release finding, not a separate fact.

rejected_candidates.detail: Part of the same peer read-through as finding 2. Molina's shrinking marketplace exposure says little about Oscar's MLR.

baseline_tension: The fundamental evidence (held-back accruals, a raise cadence, benign peer MLRs) agrees with the call-bid skew and the 16.7% run-up, so it is largely the market's own view. The one thing pointing against the skew is this name's habit of selling good prints, so p_up moves to 52 rather than the 58-60 the documents alone would justify.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the accrual/raise finding went from +2.5 to +2.0 because the Q2 beat-and-raise closed -11.86%.
Lesson 5 (narrow proxy, partly priced): the peer read-through went from +1.0 to +0.8. Centene printed before the run-up and both peers are proxies, not Oscar's own number.

Lesson 7 (sign against the skew needs a reason): the positioning negative went from -2.0 to -1.5. The skew leans up, and short interest of 2.7 days means no squeeze but also no crowded-short fuel. The reason it is kept is the Q2 reversal on the same setup.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar was confirmed from two estimate sources within $0.03 and from the company guide, so no cap was applied. The churn, 2027, overhang findings and p_up/abs_move were left unchanged.
